SMTO-SKL-0030 — Google Calendar refused this request

GUID: 4a1e403e-ef0d-5780-ac8a-f3c031fc0407
Slug: google-calendar-provider-rejected
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • Google turned down this calendar request without a reason SMTO recognizes. Google refused it, so this change wasn't made.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO again with one simple change at a time, for example change the time first, then the guests. A smaller request makes it easier to find the part Google won't accept.
  2. Open the event in Google Calendar in your browser and check that this change is offered there. If you make the change yourself, don't ask SMTO to make it too. If Google doesn't allow the change in its own app, SMTO can't make it either.
  3. If Google Calendar allows it and you still want SMTO to do it, ask again with exact details: the date, time, calendar and what to change. Exact details help SMTO send a request Google accepts.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the request and the change shows in Google Calendar.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with a description of the change you wanted, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; Google will refuse it the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Calendar returned a non-success status (typically 400) that is not classified as authentication, permission, rate limit, not-found, conflict or server unavailability.

What this means

  • Google returns a non-success status not assigned to authentication, permissions, rate limits, missing resources, conflicts or server unavailability. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns a non-success status not assigned to authentication, permissions, rate limits, missing resources, conflicts or server unavailability.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual status and safe provider detail before changing arguments.

How to fix it

  • Review the structured arguments against the google_calendar tool schema and what the Calendar API supports for that event or calendar type (event type, conferencing, attendees, reminders). Correct the request before trying again; the HTTP status is in the error details.
  • Review the structured arguments and the provider-supported event operation. Correct the request before trying again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the structured arguments and the provider-supported event operation. Correct the request before trying again.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected supported request succeeds or the provider's specific limitation is retained.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
